subject: English Language

questions.prompt: Where did Allen and Pendo travel? (A Mkangumi village, B Mkunguni town, C Mkunguni street, C Mkunguni ward, E Mkunguni village)
steps: The included page 6 script gives this destination.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: When did they reach the bus stop? (A 5:30, B 4:30, C half past six, D half to twelve, E 12:30)
steps: The script explicitly states 6:30 in the morning.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which river did the bus cross? (A Lau, B Rau, C Rua, D Lua, E Reu)
steps: The script names Rau.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where was the giraffe eating leaves? (A tall tree, B short tree, C long grasses, D short grasses, E short flower)
steps: The final script sentence gives the tree description.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which animal group did they see? (A lions/elephants/hyena, B zebras/giraffes/lions, C monkeys/lions/antelope, D elephants/giraffe/hare, E hyena/antelope/monkey)
steps: All three occur in the passage; the other options add unmentioned animals.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Two buses ___ very fast often. (A were moving, B are moving, C moves, D moved, E move)
steps: The plural subject takes move; often usually signals habitual simple present without a past context.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. Move for a current habit; D. moved is possible for a past habit.

questions.prompt: Passengers have already ___ for tickets. (A pays, B paying, C payed, D paid, E pay)
steps: Paid is the past participle for paying money.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where can I ___ the book? (A get, B gets, C got, D getting, E gotten)
steps: Can takes the base verb.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: ___ you work hard, you will not succeed. (A if, B unless, C neither, D either, E altogether)
steps: Unless means if you do not, expressing the need for effort.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of ugliest? (A beautiful, B more beautiful, C most beautiful, D beautifully, E best beautiful)
steps: Keep the superlative degree when giving the opposite.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: This is the place ___ I spend holidays. Bank: which, where, who, whom, whose.
steps: Where introduces the place clause.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: I gave her a pen ___ she put on the table.
steps: Which refers to the pen.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: This is the woman ___ child cried.
steps: Whose shows the child's relationship to the woman.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: You will see the man ___ ran away.
steps: Who is the subject relative pronoun for the man.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Do you know the girl ___ I was talking about?
steps: The girl is the object of talking about; the bank's intended remaining word is whom.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Whom (formal); who is also accepted in ordinary English.

questions.prompt: Match pity: A inflicting pain as punishment, B begin to understand, C sympathy/sorrow, D causing suffering, E searching discarded things.
steps: Pity is this feeling of compassion.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. Sympathy and sorrow for others' misfortune.

questions.prompt: Match cruel.
steps: Cruel describes unkind conduct causing suffering.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match torture.
steps: Torture is deliberate severe suffering.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Inflicting pain or suffering as punishment.

questions.prompt: Match realise.
steps: Realise means become aware.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match scavenge.
steps: Scavenge means search for usable things or food among discarded material.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. Search things others do not want.

questions.prompt: Identify the figure in The sky got as dark as the night.
steps: As...as explicitly compares sky darkness with night.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Hardly had I reached the market ___ it rained.
steps: Use hardly...when.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: If you study hard, you ___ exams.
steps: Use will plus base verb in this future condition.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Add a tag: Salome played netball last week.
steps: A positive simple-past statement takes didn't and the subject pronoun.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Salome played netball last week, didn't she?

questions.prompt: Who designs machines, bridges or roads?
steps: Engineer is the occupation described.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Suggest a title for the farewell poem.
steps: A title should reflect farewell, advice and a new stage of life.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Example: Goodbye and a New Beginning.

questions.prompt: What is the value of education in the poem?
steps: The final two lines give this value.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Being a good example wherever you are.

questions.prompt: Identify the figure in Life is like the sun.
steps: Like introduces the comparison.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is life compared with?
steps: The first line supplies the comparison.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many verses/lines are in each stanza?
steps: Count the printed lines in each grouped stanza.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Four lines in each of two stanzas.

questions.prompt: Order letter sentences A-E: I hope we meet at home in December.
steps: The hoped-for meeting closes the body.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: I wish you the best in your exams.
steps: Good wishes follow the news about the exams.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Dear Winfrida.
steps: The greeting opens the letter.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: I heard about your terminal examination in May 2024.
steps: This news follows thanks for the previous letter.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Thank you for your letter.
steps: Acknowledge the letter immediately after greeting.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening and grammar: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.
summaries.Poetry and composition: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: SPES Standard Six (VI) Monthly Exams September 2024

limitations: 1(i): Two printed choices use letter C; destination E is unambiguous.
